newsitem.title: USA: Clinton interested in "diversity" of views on Fed.
newsitem.headline: Clinton interested in "diversity" of views on Fed.

text.p: President Bill Clinton, looking to fill two vacancies on the Federal Reserve Board, is interested in having a diversity of viewpoints represented on the central bank board, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Thursday.

Asked if Clinton was looking for any particular bias, for example towards higher growth, McCurry told reporters: "I wouldn't comemt on that type of criteria in any event, because it's up to the independent Fed to make monetary policy."

Reminded of past Clinton statements suggesting that more debate was necessary within the Fed's deliberations, McCurry replied: "I think he is interested in having diversity represented within the Fed."

McCurry also echoed statements he made Thursday morning, when he suggested Clinton was "satisfied" by the two names submitted to him for the posts and that it may be several weeks before the administration formally announces them.
"He is settling in on some very excellent and highly qualified nominations and I expect probably sometime in several weeks we'll be in a positon to make formal announcements," McCurry added.

McCurry otherwise spoke only in general terms about the qualifications that Clinton sought, saying: "The president is interested in excellence in the operating of the independent Federal Reserve. He wanted people of high reputation, strong credentials and expertise to work in what is an independent governing body."
